question: A family history of adverse anaesthetic reactions — such as malignant hyperthermia in a first-degree relative — is a clinically relevant item that should be specifically asked in the pre-anaesthetic history.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Family history of malignant hyperthermia is critically important. MH is inherited (often autosomal dominant) and is life-threatening if triggering agents are used in a susceptible patient. Always ask specifically about MH and other familial anaesthetic problems.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Malignant hyperthermia has autosomal dominant inheritance; a positive family history mandates avoidance of triggering agents (volatile halogenated anaesthetics and succinylcholine) and preparation of dantrolene.
